To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Italian version of Antonovsky’s SOC Scale has been validated and the results of the first study on SOC in the Italian population are presented.

we have validated the SOC questionnaire for the Italian population, that we have presented the first SOC values for an Italian population, and that we have shown how socio demographic factors are associated with SOC.

the Italian SOC scale is a valid instrument to measure the salutogenic construct of SOC; SOC is not a linear variable, but a multidimensional construct; the SOC scale is influenced by socio-demographic variables, and the effect is not univocal.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of the SOC scale in the Italian language, and with the analysis of its properties in an Italian sample of adults, with the aim of offering a control population for comparisons with specific groups, and to provide the first data on the Italian population.
the development of the SOC questionnaire in the Italian language and the analysis of the socio-demographic patterns of SOC in a large sample of the Italian population.
the validation and cultural adaptation of the SOC scale for use in Italy, and with the statistical analysis of the effects of socio-economic variables on SOC in an Italian population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents a validated Italian version of the SOC questionnaire.
the SOC questionnaire is a valid and reliable tool to assess salutogenic aspects in the Italian population.
SOC is an important and useful concept in the field of Public Health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SOC is a useful tool in the study of salutogenesis, and that the cross-cultural adaptation of a SOC questionnaire is a valid method for the assessment of SOC in different populations.
the SOC is not only the result of the individual characteristics, but also a product of the social and cultural context.
the SOC scale can be used in Italy, and it is important to use the Italian version of the SOC scale in order to avoid cultural bias in research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Italian SOC scale is a valid instrument for measuring SOC in Italy, and that the distribution of SOC values in an Italian population is similar to that of other countries.
the SOC questionnaire is now available in Italian, and the data collected can be used to compare different Italian populations, and to identify subgroups at risk.
SOC is a valid tool to assess the salutogenic dimension of the individual and the community.
